text.text_excerpt: Daddy Hot Bird is a fried chicken pop-up that I've been wanting to try! Most recently, I got to try them at Mid-City bar Pal's and it was well worth the wait. You order at the truck and they bring the food to your table, so you don't have to wait to hear your name called. I'm not one on spice so I kept it basic with the Metairie flavoring, which had a small kick and nice flavoring. They had a whole variety of more intense spices though, so if you're searching for some Nashville hot chicken, this is your spot. The sandwich looked good, but I got the tenders which came with toasted bread and pickles - essentially the same thing you get for the sandwich just in tender form. Everything was de...

DHB is the best food truck in New Orleans. I have been visiting them since they first started operating their truck last year. They move all around the city, so be sure to check their instagram page for their location each week. I always get the DHB Sando with Uptown spice level. My first time ordering from them I got the Cluck Me Up Fam spice level and they are not lying when they say that it is HOT. I forced myself to be strong and finish the sandwich, but I certainly won't be ordering that spice level again lol. The Uptown is still very spicy, but much more manageable. I prefer to get the sandwich over the sliders because the sandwich comes with slaw, which is much needed when the chic...

Best Nashville hot chicken in NOLA!! The first time I ordered, I had the Cluck Me Up Fam DHB Sando and the Crinkle Cut Fries. The Cluck Me Up Fam spice level is insanely high, so definitely don't underestimate it. The fries were hot, fresh, and delicious. When I ordered again a few weeks later, I had the Downtown DHB Sando. It was still pretty spicy, but not so much that it overwhelmed everything else. The chicken is always super crunchy on the outside and tender on the inside. Both the slaw and pickles on the sandwich add a refreshing note to the sandwich.
